/assign @ConnorDoyle 
/cc @klueska

@zouyee Thanks for your PR. Sorry I'm just now seeing it.

Would it be possible for you to include an e2e test that fails before this fix, but succeeds after? I haven't actually run into this issue myself, so I'm curious exactly what triggers it.

It's not just a simple kubelet restart because I test this scenario manually quite often, and we also have an e2e test that verifies that the state remains in tact across kubelet restarts:  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e_node/cpu_manager_test.go#L479

I could maybe see this bug being triggered by the following sequence of events:
1) Kubelet stopped
2) API server becomes unreachable
3) Kubelet start --> State file wiped
4) API server reachable again

It would be good to have a test that verifies this though.

Also, this patch will need a rebase one https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84196 lands since the logic to remove stale state is being abstracted out into its own function.
@klueska OK

I have independently verified this issue and the proposed fix.

The issue was first introduced by the following commit and included as part of kubernetes v1.14.0: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/10995f661d0d025b6f1ed6ad0fb5c858b1b5ef76

The problematic commit adds support to garbage collect any stale state the CPUManager maintains for containers not in the `activePods` list. However, this list is typically out-of-date (e.g. empty) when a kubelet restart occurs, essentially emptying out *all* stored state for the CPUManager as it comes online.

The proposed fix makes sure that this cleanup doesn't happen until *after* the activePods list has been populated. It's worth noting that the `devicemanager` already does something similar: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/manager.go#L592

/lgtm

Let’s proceed with this change, given that it mirrors the current behavior of the device manager.

/approve
